content.comment_body: Hello! I'm looking to control six motors running via variable frequency drives using a single potentiometer as the central control point. Which [product_name] modules would be appropriate for this setup? Each motor runs at a different speed, but I want to adjust all from one location. Please advise urgently. Regards, [user_name]

This reminds me of a project completed by one of my colleagues during their studies at a university. They used these core components: 1) [product_name] Basic Unit with 8 digital inputs, 4 analog inputs, and 4 digital outputs ([article_no]), and 2) Expansion Unit with analog output (0-10 V) ([article_no]). Inputs were used for start and stop functions. The potentiometer was wired to the analog input, an output enabled the drive, and another controlled start/stop. An analog output provided the speed reference for the drive.

Hello, does this mean I would need three analog input expansion modules to control six motors, since one analog output seems to manage only two motors? The rest of your explanation makes sense. Thank you, [user_name]

Hi! I believe you can address this by programming the drives. If the drives use voltage as their analog input, you can apply the same voltage signal in parallel to all six drives and then set each drive’s parameters individually to achieve the required speeds. For [product_name] [version_no], you only have two analog outputs available.

Hello, In fact, we used to synchronize machines in a production line this way: generating a 0-10V signal, typically from a main controller, then distributing it to all downstream equipment. Precise programming, such as setting ramps and end frequencies carefully, is important for maintaining speed synchronization. Some important notes: • not all drive analog inputs are galvanically isolated • ensure the voltage source provides adequate current for all connections • route analogue signals properly with suitable cabling.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discuss controlling six variable frequency drives using a single potentiometer and [product_name] modules for centralized analog control. The thread highlights hardware limitations, including the available number of analog outputs, and leads to questions about module selection needed for multiple motor control. Parallel analog output distribution, drive input isolation, and proper analog wiring practices are identified as key considerations.
analysis.user_expectations: Users anticipate an easy solution for centralized control of six motors using [product_name] modules and hope for clear guidance on module selection to achieve this configuration.
